proposed_english: to smite / to strike (deal a wounding blow)
rationale: Recurring verb in this kephalaion (lines 1, 2, 12) governing the action of the judge/enemy inflicting a wound. Likely Lycopolitan striking-verb related to ϣⲣⲁϩ 'afflict' or ϣⲱϣ 'smite.' The medical-judicial context (paired with πληγή 'plague/blow') and the typology 'wound-at-place-of-wound' confirms 'smite/strike' as the action that produces a ϣϭⲁ ('wound,' line 3, 6). Distinct from ⲡⲱⲍ 'wound/breach' (in glossary).

Standard Manichaean cosmological figure — the cosmic Judge who recompenses an enemy for sins committed against the innocent by inflicting a corresponding sickness. Distinct from ⲡⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲧⲙⲏⲉ 'Judge of Truth' (in glossary): this 'Judge of the cosmos' operates within the manifest world to enforce the cosmic justice of recompense (ϣⲃⲓⲱ). Greek κριτής τοῦ κόσμου.

Greek loanword μοῖρα 'allotted lot, portion, fated share.' Used here in the construction ϯ-ⲙⲱⲣⲏ 'give a portion' — the Judge of the cosmos gives each one his appointed share in the recompense-economy. Standard cosmological-judicial term.

Greek loanword ἀντίδικος 'opponent at law, adversary.' Variant orthography of ⲁⲛⲧⲓⲁⲕⲟⲥ already in accumulated vocabulary. Here in the judicial register: the enemy who has wounded the innocent man and is brought before the Judge.

Compound: ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix 'do') + ⲡⲓ- (demonstrative 'this') + ⲍⲱⲃ ('work,' = ϩⲱⲃ in glossary). The phrase ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ-ⲣ̄-ⲡⲓⲍⲱⲃ 'because he has done this work' is standard Coptic syntax for completed action. Used here of the physician completing his medical task.

Lycopolitan ⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ = Sahidic ⲙⲁⲉⲓⲛ 'sign, mark, distinguishing feature.' Adverbial usage with prefixed ⲙ̄- = 'as signs.' The wounds inflicted by the enemy serve as visible signs/marks on the body that condemn him before the Judge.

Compound: ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲟⲩϣϭⲁ ('a wound'). Used in the recompense-formula 'wound at the place of a wound, blow at the place of a blow' — direct correspondence between original injury and its recompense. Standard Coptic ⲙⲁⲛ- compound (cf. ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲟⲣⲉ, ⲙⲁⲛⲣⲁⲓⲥ, etc.).

Recurring noun in this kephalaion (lines 1, 6) for the bodily wound inflicted by the smiting blow. Distinct from ⲡⲱⲍ 'breach/wound' (glossary) and πληγή 'plague/blow.' Possibly Lyc. variant or specialized lexeme for a specific injury-type. Forms the wound/place-of-wound recompense-pair.

Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲧⲁⲗϭⲉ/ⲧⲁⲗϭⲟ 'healing, cure.' Without the ⲧⲁⲗ- prefix here. Used in 'the healing of his sickness' (line 13). Cf. accumulated ⲡⲗⲅⲟ/ⲧⲗⲅⲟ 'healing/curing' — same root, different prefixation.

Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲧⲱⲕ 'trust, confidence' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲉϩⲧⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'cheering of his heart' which uses related ⲧⲱⲕ). Used here in 'trust to him to examine the plague' — the patient's reliance on the physician. Confidence moderate.
Lyc. reflex of ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'cast, throw' (cf. accumulated ⲛⲁⲝϥ̄ 'cast him'). Used here in juridical sense 'cast blame upon someone' in the negation 'they cast no (blame) upon him' (line 20).
